title: Element Style Contract
description: Per-element (and per-run) expected computed-style assertions, added as optional fields on element-manifest.json element entries. verify_elements.py compares `style`/`runs[].style` against the measured DOM computed styles produced by measure_dom_elements.cjs and emits a per-property delta — the repair worklist. This is the machine version of 'compare against the spec value', replacing 'eyeball the screenshot and tweak CSS'. All fields are OPTIONAL and additive: an element without `style` is verified exactly as before (presence/geometry/text/type).
description_attachment: This schema describes the OPTIONAL additions to an element-manifest element entry. An element entry MAY carry `style` (single-style text or a surface) and/or `runs` (composite typography: number+unit+suffix etc.). When `runs` is present, the element's existing `content` MUST equal the concatenation of runs[].text, and each run is asserted independently.

runs.description: Composite-typography breakdown of a single text element. Codegen renders one node per run carrying data-run="<element-id>.<index>"; measure_dom_elements.cjs measures each [data-run] node's computed style; verify_elements.py asserts each run's style independently. join(runs[].text) MUST equal the element's content.

color.description: Expected color as #rrggbb (sRGB). The DOM side converts getComputedStyle rgb(...) to hex before comparison.

expectedStyle.description: Resolved expected computed-style values (what the verifier compares against). Every value present here should also appear in token_refs unless source is 'measured' or 'declared'.

font_size_px.description: Expected rendered font-size in CSS px.

font_weight.description: Numeric weight 100-900. Named weights (normal=400, bold=700) are normalized on both sides before compare. Catches the `<strong>` default-700 leak.

line_height_px.description: Expected line-height in px (resolve unitless/em to px).

vertical_align.description: The 'baseline' axis: sub/super are what make CO₂e a subscript instead of inline body text.

font_family.description: Optional; matched loosely (first family token, case-insensitive) because system font substitution is expected.

tolerance.description: Per-property tolerance overrides for THIS element/run. Omitted properties fall back to verify_elements.py defaults (font_size_px 1.0, font_weight 0=exact, color_rgb_max 8, line_height_px 2.0, letter_spacing_px 0.5, border_radius_px 2.0). Use tolerance, not deletion, to relax an assertion.

color_rgb_max.description: Max per-channel |dR|,|dG|,|dB| in 0-255. (Simple, consistent with pixel_diff tolerance; CIEDE2000 is a future option.)

style.description: A single computed-style assertion for an element or a run.

token_refs.description: Provenance: which design token each expected property resolved from, e.g. {"font_size_px": "stat-number", "color": "ink-900"}. Keys are expectedStyle property names; values are tokens.typography/colors names in the blueprint. Enforces the 'styles come from tokens, not literals' rule.

source.description: Where the expected values came from. measured: read from the reference (DOM/pixel sampling). token: resolved from a design token. vlm-hint: VLM size/weight estimate quantized to the nearest typography token (the F3 path — VLM estimates per-run typography, no per-run bitmap OCR needed). declared: project-convention default.

severity.description: fail: a tolerance breach is a verification problem (contributes to status 'failed'). warn: reported in style_delta but does not fail the element (use for font_family / low-confidence properties).

run.description: One typographic run inside a composite text element.

text.description: This run's exact visible text. join over runs == element.content.

role.description: Semantic role from VLM perception; drives the rendered tag/class (e.g. suffix+sub -> <sub>).

examples._comment: carbon-stat value '128 kg CO₂e' — the defect case. Three runs, each with its own asserted style; the suffix is small + subscript so it does not overflow-clip, and weights are explicit so the <strong> default-700 cannot leak.
a single-style heading element using a tolerance override on color.
